finalText:
**Merge** creates new commit that joins two branches. History shows both branches existed, parallel work visible. Fast-forward if target hasn't moved since your branch started.

**Rebase** replays your commits on top of target branch. Rewrites history—looks like linear sequence, no branching. Commits get new hashes (destructive if pushed).

**When to use each:**

**Merge:**
- Shared/public branches (main, release, team work). History matters. No force-push risk.
- Feature complete, ready to document the integration point.
- Coordinating with others—rebase would rewrite their copy.

**Rebase:**
- Local branch before push. Clean history before merging to main.
- Sync with upstream without merge commits cluttering log.
- Single author, haven't pushed yet (or only to your own fork).

**Rule:** Rebase locally. Merge to shared branches. Never rebase after push (unless you own that branch).

Merge keeps truth: "this work happened in parallel." Rebase rewrites for clean narrative: "feature built on current main." Pick based on whether history matters to your team or if clean linear log is worth the risk.
